ch06.f.d.mode: Increase a horizontal pull steadily, or tilt the board steadily
ch06.f.d.mat: Materials of block and surface: they set the static coefficient $\mu_s$ and the kinetic coefficient $\mu_k$
ch06.f.goal.static: Static friction: only as large as needed, at most $\mu_s N$
ch06.f.goal.kinetic: When the block starts to slide, friction drops to $\mu_k N$ ($\mu_k < \mu_s$) and stays there
ch06.f.obs.match: At rest: the $f$ curve lies on the pull $F$ (dashed), $f_s = F$
ch06.f.obs.drop: When $f$ reaches $\mu_s N$ the block starts to slide, $f$ drops to $\mu_k N$ and $v$ starts to grow
ch06.f.obs.angle: Tilting board: sliding starts at the angle with $\tan\theta_c = \mu_s$ (wood 26.6°, ice 5.7°), whatever the mass
ch06.f.obs.mat: On the incline $N = mg\cos\theta$, so $\mu_s N$ shrinks as the angle grows
ch06.f.assume: Block mass 2 kg, the pull grows at 4 N/s, the board tilts at 6°/s and is held at the angle where sliding starts, typical friction coefficients
ch06.c.d.preset: Four situations in which different real forces keep the object on the circle
ch06.c.d.cut: The string breaks after a quarter turn
ch06.c.d.ice: Road friction vanishes after a quarter turn
ch06.c.goal.net: Uniform circular motion: the net force points to the centre and has size $mv^2/r$
ch06.c.goal.notnew: Centripetal force = the radial component of the net force. It is not a new kind of force; tension, friction or a normal force plays that role
ch06.c.obs.string: Ball on a string: the tension $T$ is the centripetal force; gravity and the normal force cancel
ch06.c.obs.flat: Flat curve: static friction $f_s$ is the centripetal force
ch06.c.obs.tilt: Banked curve and conical pendulum: the horizontal component of the tilted force ($N\sin\theta$, $T\sin\theta$) is the centripetal force; the vertical component balances $mg$
ch06.c.obs.cut: Cut string or icy road: once the inward force is gone the object moves straight along the tangent; without an inward net force there is no circular motion
ch06.c.assume: Ball on a string: 0.5 kg, radius 1 m, 3 m/s, frictionless table. Curves: 1000 kg, radius 20 m, flat curve at 10 m/s, banked curve at 20° at its design speed (no friction). Conical pendulum: 1 m string at 30°. The top views share one drawn radius; force arrows are scaled relative to $mg$
